quests.hint: Finishing two tasks by doing just one single action.
quests.explanation: One thrown stone hitting two birds pictures a single effort solving two problems at once.
quests.meaning: To achieve two goals with a single action.
quests.sampleUsage: I walked to work today, killing two birds with one stone: exercise and saving money.
quests.correctAnswer: Kill two birds with one stone
quests.expression: Kill two birds with one stone
quests.textToSpeak: Kill two birds with one stone

quests.hint: Advice to deal with a problem only once it actually happens.
quests.explanation: You don't need to plan how to cross a bridge that's still far ahead of you.
quests.meaning: To deal with a problem only when it actually occurs, not before.
quests.sampleUsage: I'm not sure what I'll do if the flight is delayed; I'll cross that bridge when I come to it.
quests.correctAnswer: Cross that bridge when you come to it
quests.expression: Cross that bridge when you come to it
quests.textToSpeak: Cross that bridge when you come to it

quests.hint: A colorful way to describe feeling very jealous of someone.
quests.explanation: Green has long been linked to sickness and jealousy in English, going back to Shakespeare's plays.
quests.meaning: Feeling very jealous of someone.
quests.sampleUsage: My coworkers were green with envy when I told them about my beach vacation.

quests.hint: Refusing to choose a side in a disagreement or decision.
quests.explanation: A fence sits exactly between two sides, so staying on it means picking neither.
quests.meaning: To avoid choosing a side in an argument or decision.
quests.sampleUsage: He kept sitting on the fence instead of telling us which restaurant he preferred.

quests.hint: Being extremely careful with your words around someone who's upset.
quests.explanation: Eggshells crack under the lightest step, matching how carefully you must tread.
quests.meaning: To be very careful about what you say or do, so as not to upset someone.
quests.sampleUsage: Ever since the argument, we've all been walking on eggshells around her.

quests.hint: A dream or plan that probably will never actually come true.
quests.explanation: A pie floating in the sky is a sweet image you can imagine but never actually taste.
quests.meaning: An idea or plan that is unrealistic and unlikely to happen.
quests.sampleUsage: His plan to retire at thirty sounds like pie in the sky to me.

quests.hint: Saying it's too late now, because the chance has already passed.
quests.explanation: Once a ship leaves the harbour, you can't board it, just like a missed opportunity.
quests.meaning: A chance or opportunity has already passed and cannot be taken now.
quests.sampleUsage: I thought about applying for that job, but that ship has sailed.

quests.hint: One image can explain something better than a long description could.
quests.explanation: It highlights how much meaning a single visual can hold compared to spoken or written explanation.
quests.meaning: A single image can express an idea more powerfully than a lot of text.
quests.sampleUsage: Just look at her face in that photo; a picture is worth a thousand words.
quests.correctAnswer: A picture is worth a thousand words
quests.expression: A picture is worth a thousand words
quests.textToSpeak: A picture is worth a thousand words

quests.hint: Acting immediately while the timing and conditions are perfect.
quests.explanation: A blacksmith can only shape iron while it's still glowing hot from the fire.
quests.meaning: To act immediately while the conditions are favourable.
quests.sampleUsage: They offered a discount today only, so we struck while the iron was hot and bought it.
quests.correctAnswer: Strike while the iron is hot
quests.expression: Strike while the iron is hot
quests.textToSpeak: Strike while the iron is hot

quests.hint: Advice not to celebrate a result before it has actually happened.
quests.explanation: An egg might never hatch into a chick, so counting future chickens too soon is risky.
quests.meaning: Don't assume something will succeed before it actually has.
quests.sampleUsage: We're leading by ten points, but let's not count our chickens before they hatch.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't count your chickens before they hatch
quests.expression: Don't count your chickens before they hatch
quests.textToSpeak: Don't count your chickens before they hatch

quests.hint: Everyone gets their own moment of success eventually.
quests.explanation: It's an old, encouraging saying that even the underdog eventually gets a turn to shine.
quests.meaning: Everyone will have a moment of success or luck at some point.
quests.sampleUsage: She finally got promoted after years of trying; every dog has its day.

quests.hint: Staying positive even when things are difficult.
quests.explanation: Lifting your chin makes your posture look confident, unlike the slumped look of sadness.
quests.meaning: To stay cheerful and confident during a difficult time.
quests.sampleUsage: I know the exam results were disappointing, but keep your chin up.

quests.hint: Someone who can do a little bit of everything.
quests.explanation: 'Jack' was once a generic name for an ordinary workman skilled at many small trades.
quests.meaning: A person who can do many different jobs reasonably well.
quests.sampleUsage: Our handyman is a real jack of all trades; he fixes plumbing, wiring, and furniture.

quests.hint: Starting a plan over again from the very beginning.
quests.explanation: Engineers literally return to their drawing board to redesign a plan that didn't work.
quests.meaning: To start a plan again from the beginning because the last attempt failed.
quests.sampleUsage: The prototype broke during testing, so it's back to the drawing board for the design team.

quests.hint: Advice not to form an opinion based only on how something looks.
quests.explanation: A book's cover tells you little about the story inside, just like first impressions.
quests.meaning: Don't form an opinion about someone or something based only on appearance.
quests.sampleUsage: He looks strict, but don't judge a book by its cover; he's actually very kind.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't judge a book by its cover
quests.expression: Don't judge a book by its cover
quests.textToSpeak: Don't judge a book by its cover

quests.hint: A funny old way to say it's raining extremely hard.
quests.explanation: Nobody is fully sure why, but this old British phrase has described heavy rain for centuries.
quests.meaning: It is raining very heavily.
quests.sampleUsage: Grab an umbrella, it's raining cats and dogs out there.

quests.hint: A child who is very similar to one of their parents.
quests.explanation: A wood chip carved from a larger block naturally shares the same grain and character.
quests.meaning: A person who resembles one of their parents in character or behaviour.
quests.sampleUsage: He loves fixing engines just like his dad; a real chip off the old block.
quests.correctAnswer: A chip off the old block
quests.expression: A chip off the old block
quests.textToSpeak: A chip off the old block

quests.hint: An extra good thing added on top of something already great.
quests.explanation: Icing sits on top of an already finished cake, adding a final, sweet touch.
quests.meaning: An additional good thing that makes an already good situation even better.
quests.sampleUsage: The food was great, and the live music was the icing on the cake.

quests.hint: Something that has both a helpful side and a harmful side.
quests.explanation: A sword sharp on both edges can cut its user just as easily as its target.
quests.meaning: Something that has both good and bad consequences.
quests.sampleUsage: Working from home is a double-edged sword; it's flexible, but it can get lonely.

quests.hint: Two people who are extremely alike or always together.
quests.explanation: Peas from the same pod look almost identical, just like two closely matched people.
quests.meaning: Two people who are very similar or very close.
quests.sampleUsage: Ever since school, my best friend and I have been like two peas in a pod.

quests.hint: Discovered in the exact moment of doing something wrong.
quests.explanation: It likely refers to a criminal caught with blood, literally red hands, still on them.
quests.meaning: Caught in the act of doing something wrong.
quests.sampleUsage: The cat was caught red-handed with its paw in the fish bowl.

quests.hint: Something interesting that makes you think about it afterwards.
quests.explanation: Just as food feeds the body, an interesting idea gives your mind something to 'chew on.'
quests.meaning: Something worth thinking about seriously.
quests.sampleUsage: Her comment about saving more each month gave me some food for thought.

quests.hint: Doing or saying something to make a group feel more comfortable at the start.
quests.explanation: Ships once had to break thick ice to move forward, just as a joke clears social tension.
quests.meaning: To do or say something to relieve tension or make people feel comfortable.
quests.sampleUsage: He told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.

quests.hint: Losing your chance because you were too slow to act.
quests.explanation: If you arrive after a boat has already left the dock, there's no catching up to it.
quests.meaning: To miss an opportunity by acting too slowly.
quests.sampleUsage: Tickets sold out this morning, so we missed the boat on front-row seats.

quests.hint: A simple way to describe something that's extremely expensive.
quests.explanation: A 'fortune' means a large amount of money, so the price is compared to an entire fortune.
quests.meaning: To be very expensive.
quests.sampleUsage: Renovating the kitchen cost a fortune, but it was worth it.

quests.hint: Starting a process or activity that will then keep moving forward.
quests.explanation: Once a rolling ball has momentum, it keeps moving on its own, just like a started project.
quests.meaning: To start something happening.
quests.sampleUsage: Let's get the ball rolling on the project by assigning everyone a task today.

quests.hint: Telling someone honestly and directly how angry you are with them.
quests.explanation: You're sharing a direct, unfiltered part of your thoughts, exactly as they are.
quests.meaning: To tell someone directly and honestly that you are angry with them.
quests.sampleUsage: When the delivery was late again, she gave the driver a piece of her mind.

quests.hint: Waiting until the next day before deciding something important.
quests.explanation: A night of rest often brings a clearer head than deciding in a rushed moment.
quests.meaning: To wait until the next day before making a decision.
quests.sampleUsage: It's a big offer, so take some time and sleep on it before you reply.

quests.hint: What you say when someone appears right after you were talking about them.
quests.explanation: It's a shortened, friendlier version of an old superstition that naming the devil might summon him.
quests.meaning: Said when a person who was just being discussed suddenly appears.
quests.sampleUsage: Speak of the devil, we were just talking about you and your new job!

quests.hint: It's still good that something happened, even though it happened late.
quests.explanation: The phrase gently accepts a delay by comparing it to the far worse alternative: nothing at all.
quests.meaning: It is better for something to happen late than not to happen at all.
quests.sampleUsage: He finally replied to my message after two weeks; well, better late than never.
